intro: Build a polynomial or rational function from its factors. Drag a factor's pin along the $x$-axis, give it a multiplicity, or move it to the denominator. The graph, the sign chart and every feature update together: zeros that cross or touch, vertical asymptotes with both one-sided limits, holes where a factor cancels, and the end behavior in limit notation.
howItWorksTitle: How the features are read from the factors
howItWorks:
• Zeros. A factor $(x - a)^m$ in the numerator gives a zero at $x = a$. Odd $m$: the graph crosses the $x$-axis (flattening when $m \ge 3$). Even $m$: it touches and turns back.
  • Vertical asymptotes. A factor left in the denominator after canceling. Each side gets its own limit: $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x)$ and $\lim_{x \to a^+} f(x)$, each $\infty$ or $-\infty$, found from the signs of the other factors.
  • Holes. A factor that cancels (top and bottom) leaves a hole: $f(a)$ is undefined, but the graph approaches one height there.
  • End behavior. Compare degrees. Numerator higher: no horizontal asymptote, and the limits at $\pm\infty$ are $\infty$ or $-\infty$ (a slant asymptote when it is higher by exactly one). Equal: $y$ = the ratio of the leading coefficients. Denominator higher: $y = 0$.
  • Sign chart. The sign can change only at a zero of odd multiplicity or an asymptote of odd power; a hole never changes it.
  • Keyboard: each pin is a slider (arrow keys move it by 0.5, Shift by 5).
